Definition: What proportion of businesses does the register cover?
Comments: No credible evidence found for proportion; formal sector low.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Cameroon's Ministry of SMEs 2024 Statistical Yearbook, citing the National Institute of Statistics' second General Business Census (RGE-2), reports only 62,902 formal, properly-structured businesses (14.6% of the c.430,000 business stock) and 95.7% of the c.3.7 million informal production units lacking a tax number, with 97.4% unregistered in the trade register (2024 data). This supports <20% coverage; original Value Code confirmed, now with an authoritative source.

revision_notes: Revised. No nationwide separate digital cadastre exists (2020 academic study confirms Cameroon lacked a modern cadastral system), but MINDCAF signed an MOU in August 2025 to pilot digitisation of cadastral/land procedures in Lékié Division, and a separate 'multipurpose cadastre' pilot in Soa commune had, per a March 2026 MINDCAF release, already field-identified 20,000 titled parcels over 330km². This is active piloting rather than 'No'; changed from 1 to 3 (Under development).

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital population register?
Comments: No credible evidence found after searching for Cameroon population register, national population register digital, BUCREP digital register, civil register of persons, World Bank ID4D dataset, UN CRVS reports, e-government portals. BUCREP handles census and estimates but no digital population register mentioned; civil register is separate.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Cameroon has no continuously-updated population register distinct from its civil registration system (CRVS, run by BUNEC) or its census/demographic-studies body (BUCREP, per its own 'about' page, conducts censuses and surveys rather than maintaining a live population register). The 2024 civil-registration reform law creates a National Civil Status Database and Unique Personal Identification Number, but this is a vital-events (CRVS) register targeted for full digitisation only by 2029, not a population register. No=1 confirmed.

revision_notes: Confirmed.
